Aurora Metals Appoints Industry Veteran as New CEO to Drive Expansion

TORONTO, June 14 — Aurora Metals Inc., a leading Canadian producer of base and precious metals, announced Thursday the appointment of Christine DeLuca as its new chief executive officer, effective July 1. DeLuca, who brings more than two decades of experience in the mining sector, will replace outgoing CEO Peter McDonnell, who is retiring after nine years at the helm.

The Toronto-based company cited DeLuca’s proven leadership and extensive background in mine operations, project development, and sustainability initiatives as key factors in her selection.

“Christine’s track record of delivering operational excellence and her commitment to responsible mining make her the ideal leader for Aurora Metals as we look to expand our footprint in Canada and abroad,” said Chairperson Samuel Yeh in a statement. “Her experience will be invaluable as we continue to advance our pipeline of projects and enhance value for our stakeholders.”

DeLuca previously served as Chief Operating Officer at North Ridge Resources, where she oversaw the development of two major copper and nickel mines in northern Quebec. She has also held senior roles with several mining firms across Canada and Latin America.

“I am honoured to join Aurora Metals at such a pivotal time for the industry,” DeLuca said in the company’s release. “With increasing demand for responsibly sourced metals, especially those critical to the global energy transition, Aurora is well-positioned for sustainable growth. I look forward to working with our talented team to advance our projects, strengthen relationships with local communities, and deliver results for our shareholders.”

Industry analysts welcomed the appointment, noting DeLuca’s strong reputation for operational efficiency and stakeholder engagement. “Christine DeLuca is well respected in the sector and her hands-on approach will likely help Aurora Metals navigate both the opportunities and challenges facing the Canadian mining industry,” said Emily Fraser, mining analyst at Dominion Equity Group.

Aurora Metals operates mines in Ontario, Quebec and British Columbia, producing copper, nickel, zinc and gold. The company is currently developing the Bear Lake nickel-copper project in northern Ontario, slated to begin production in 2026. According to public filings, Aurora Metals posted revenues of CAD 2.1 billion in 2023.

The Mining Association of Canada welcomed the news, citing DeLuca’s support for industry-wide sustainability initiatives. “We look forward to working with Christine in her new role and continuing our collaboration on advancing responsible mining practices across Canada,” said MAC President Pierre Giroux.

Shares in Aurora Metals rose 1.3% on the Toronto Stock Exchange following the announcement.
